title: Daily exercise for dogs
text: Adult dogs need at least 30 to 60 minutes of walking or active play every day. Without it they often develop destructive behaviour, weight gain and anxiety.

title: Puppy care
text: Puppies under one year need several short potty breaks, short training sessions of 5 to 10 minutes, and gentle socialization. Walks should be short because their joints are still growing.

title: Senior dog joint care
text: Dogs aged 8 and older benefit from shorter, gentler walks twice a day and joint supplements as advised by a vet. Watch for stiffness, limping and slowing down.

title: Dental care
text: Brushing a dog or cat's teeth several times a week prevents tartar and gum disease, which is linked to heart and kidney problems.

title: Dog feeding schedule
text: Adult dogs do best with two measured meals a day, about 12 hours apart. Fresh water must always be available.

title: Coat and nail care
text: Brush dogs weekly (daily for long coats) and trim nails every 3 to 4 weeks. Overgrown nails cause pain and change how a dog walks.

title: Play and enrichment for cats
text: Indoor cats need two or more play sessions of 10 to 15 minutes daily, ideally with a wand toy that mimics hunting. This prevents boredom, obesity and scratching problems.

title: Litter box hygiene
text: Scoop the litter box at least once a day. A dirty box is a leading cause of cats refusing to use it and can hide early signs of urinary illness.

title: Cat feeding and water
text: Adult cats do well on two measured meals daily, with wet food helping hydration. Refresh water daily.

title: Senior cat monitoring
text: Cats aged 11 and older should have their weight, appetite and water intake checked regularly, since kidney disease and hyperthyroidism are common. Gentle play keeps joints mobile.

title: Cat brushing
text: Brushing a cat a few times a week reduces hairballs and shedding, and lets you spot lumps or skin problems early.

title: Diabetes and insulin
text: Diabetic pets need insulin at the same times every day, usually 12 hours apart, given with a meal. A missed or late dose can cause dangerous blood sugar swings, so it is never optional.

title: Allergies and skin care
text: Pets with allergies need any prescribed medication given on schedule and regular wiping of paws and coat after outdoor time to remove pollen.

recommendation.title: Give allergy medication and wipe paws

title: Arthritis and mobility
text: Pets with arthritis or hip problems need pain relief or supplements as prescribed, low-impact exercise, and soft bedding. Avoid jumping and long runs.

title: Anxiety and calming routines
text: Anxious pets cope better with predictable routines, a quiet safe space and daily calm one-to-one time. Exercise before stressful events helps.

title: Small pets and exotics
text: Small pets need fresh water and food daily, spot cleaning of the habitat every day and a full clean weekly. Rabbits also need unlimited hay and daily time out of the cage.
